great_northern_war.note: Great Northern War chronology and destructive campaigning across the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

great_northern_plague.note: The plague associated with the Great Northern War peaked in Baltic/East-Central Europe around 1708–1712.

war_polish_succession.note: The War of the Polish Succession included the 1734 siege of Gdańsk.

bar_confederation.note: Bar Confederation fighting and Russian intervention affected multiple Commonwealth regions.

partitions.note: The partitions occurred in 1772, 1793 and 1795; the game derives affected places from its Town polity timeline.

napoleonic.note: Duchy of Warsaw/Napoleonic campaigns and 1812 Russian campaign.

november_uprising.note: After the 1830–31 uprising, participants faced imprisonment, confiscation, exile and emigration.

galicia_1846.note: Kraków uprising and Galician peasant violence.

greater_poland_1848.note: Greater Poland uprising during the Revolutions of 1848.

january_uprising.note: The 1863–64 uprising and subsequent Russian repression included executions, exile and confiscation.

revolution_1905.note: The 1905 revolution in Congress Poland included strikes and violent confrontations, especially in industrial centres.

ww1.note: WWI fighting, requisitions and economic disruption across Polish lands.

great_retreat.note: 1915 Russian retreat involved large-scale civilian evacuation/refugee movement.

spanish_flu.note: Poland experienced three major influenza waves in 1918–1920; published estimates place deaths in the hundreds of thousands.

polish_ukrainian_war.note: 1918–19 Polish-Ukrainian fighting centered on Eastern Galicia/Lwów.

great_depression.note: The Depression brought severe unemployment and industrial contraction in Poland.

flood_1934.note: The 1934 southern Poland flood caused major building and agricultural damage.

invasion_1939.note: German and Soviet invasions in 1939 produced mass civilian displacement, destruction and casualties.

ww2_occupation.note: General German/Soviet occupation hardship; local persecution events are modeled separately at higher priority.

soviet_deportations.note: Four mass Soviet deportation waves in 1940–41 affected hundreds of thousands of Polish citizens; targeted groups included military settlers, officials, forest and railway workers and their families.

holocaust.note: German authorities confined Jews in ghettos and, from 1942, deported and murdered the overwhelming majority in killing centers and mass shootings.

volhynia.note: 1943–44 mass anti-Polish violence in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia caused mass killing and flight; retaliatory Polish violence against Ukrainians is represented at lower scale.

warsaw_uprising.note: The Warsaw Uprising ended with enormous civilian casualties, civilian deportation and destruction of most of the city.

postwar_resettlement.note: Postwar borders drove mass population transfers: Poles from eastern territories to postwar Poland and Germans from territories transferred to Poland.

operation_vistula.note: In 1947 more than 140,000 Ukrainians were forcibly resettled from southeastern Poland to western/northern territories.

territorial_exchange_1951.note: 1951 Polish–Soviet territorial exchange required population removals from the exchanged areas.

poznan_1956.note: Poznań June worker protests were violently suppressed, with deaths, injuries and arrests.

march_1968.note: The state anti-Jewish campaign caused purges and about 13,000 Jews to leave Poland.

december_1970.note: Coastal worker protests in Gdańsk, Gdynia, Elbląg and Szczecin were violently suppressed; IPN gives 44 official deaths, more than 1,000 injuries and more than 2,000 arrests.

june_1976.note: June 1976 worker protests centered on Radom, Ursus and Płock.

solidarity_1980.note: 1980 strike wave led to the Gdańsk Agreements and Solidarity.

martial_law.note: During martial law, roughly ten thousand people were interned; industrial confrontations included lethal violence.

market_transition.note: The 1989–93 transition involved rapid restructuring and rising unemployment; effect rates are gameplay abstractions.

flood_1997.note: The 1997 flood killed 56 people in Poland; thousands lost homes or belongings and property damage was extensive.

eu_migration.note: EU accession in May 2004 triggered one of Poland's largest postwar emigration waves, especially to the UK and Ireland.

flood_2010.note: The 2010 floods affected southern/eastern Poland, required about 30,000 evacuations and caused very large property/agricultural losses.

covid.note: The COVID-19 pandemic produced exceptionally high mortality in Poland in 2020–21, especially among older people.

ukraine_refugees.note: Following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, more than two million arrivals from Ukraine entered Poland within the first three weeks; the game models this as a temporary generated-outsider modifier.

flood_2024.note: September 2024 flooding caused severe damage in Lower Silesia and Opole, including Kłodzko, Nysa and Głuchołazy.
